Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful intro to Redwood's hosted offering. As we discussed, the next step on our side is to lock down expected monthly token volume and peak TPS so we can validate the cost model with our finance team. A few clarifying items: 

- Our initial MVP (chat + summarization) is expected to process roughly 1.5M user messages/month. We estimate ~8k tokens per user session on average (prompt + response), but this is still a rough number.
- Peak traffic window: ~11am–1pm PST, expected peak TPS around 35–40 calls/s (chat calls). Burst tolerance up to ~70 TPS for short periods.
- Target unit economics: we need to model target spend around $1k–$5k/month to start for a pilot, but longer-term we want to see ~$10–20 per 1M tokens or equivalent pricing to make the model viable. Can you confirm: what is Redwood's hosted API pricing bands for this volume and any discounts or committed pricing? Also — do you recommend Dedicated or Hosted for this pattern?

Appreciate a short recap we can share with finance.

Thanks,
Ana Torres
Head of AI Product

Hi Ana — great to meet you on the call. Quick recap and answers to your bullets below.

Recap / answers:
- Monthly volume: 1.5M messages x ~8k tokens/session -> rough ballpark 12B tokens/month. If you expect these numbers to move, send over the usage_projection.xlsx and we can iterate.
- Peak TPS: 35–40 TPS sustained in the noon window, with bursts up to ~70 TPS. For Hosted API, we can support that with autoscaling, but sustained high TPS (especially low-latency <100ms SLO) could benefit from a Dedicated commit.
- Pricing: Hosted API base rates depend on model selection (open vs. Redwood-optimized). As a starting estimate for budgeting: 
  - Standard open-model band: $30–$60 per 1M tokens (depends on model and quantization).
  - Redwood-verified/recommended model variants: $15–$35 per 1M tokens depending on committed volume / tier.
  - We can discuss committed pricing if you plan >50B tokens/month — that moves into Dedicated/reserved pricing with lower unit costs.

Given your initial pilot budget target ($1k–$5k/month), that budget maps to ~33M–166M tokens/month at $30/1M tokens — which is well below the 12B token estimate above. If your MVP truly needs 12B tokens/month, the pilot spend will be in the low-to-mid five figures on Hosted. Two quick options:
  1) Reduce model size/sequence length and use aggressive quantization / caching — reduces token consumption and per-token compute.
  2) Start with a narrow user cohort (beta) to align pilot spend to your $1k–$5k target, and scale after validation.

Next steps I recommend:
- Can you confirm whether the 8k tokens/session is avg or 95th percentile?
- Share the usage_projection.xlsx (or we can run a short calc on our side)
- I can loop in Rishi (SE) to outline latency and throughput guidance for Hosted vs Dedicated + a quick cost back-of-envelope based on model choice.

For transparency: I'll put a small spreadsheet together showing cost bands for 1M / 100M / 1B token buckets so you have clear $/1M numbers at different scales.

Best,

Hi Ana — quick SE note on the throughput and deployment recommendation.

Thanks for the detailed numbers — a couple of calibration points: 
- 8k tokens/session implies fairly long prompts/responses. If those are mostly response-side tokens (model-generated), batching and prefix/KV caching can reduce compute in many cases. If they are prompt-heavy (long context per call), that has larger cost implications.
- For sustained 35–40 TPS with 70 TPS bursts, Hosted can handle this but you may see higher tail latencies during bursts unless you have dedicated pool capacity. If your SLO target is <=150ms p90, I'd recommend Dedicated (or a Hosted-to-Dedicated bridge) for the production rollout.

Estimated costs (very rough hosted estimates using Redwood-verified model X):
- 1M tokens => $25 per 1M tokens (model X, mid-tier)
- 100M tokens => $22 per 1M tokens (volume effect)
- 1B tokens => $18 per 1M tokens (committed/discounted)

I've attached a short usage_projection.xlsx with a few scenarios (pilot / 6-month scale / full rollout) and an assumed $/1M band. It also includes a simple TPS->GPU capacity mapping so you can see when Dedicated becomes cost-effective.

Attachment: usage_projection.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If it's helpful, we can run a short PoC on Hosted for the beta (with conservative model sizing) and then switch to Dedicated when you cross the throughput/volume threshold — we can map break-even points in the spreadsheet.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
